create_nuclear_industry.ponder.experimen: Experimental Reactor: Build
This 5×5×5 example can extend to 5–16 blocks on each side; every edge must use reactor casing.
Arrange fuel and control-rod columns freely; unused columns may stay empty.
Fill each fuel column through the full internal height and cap it with a refueling port.
Leave control-rod columns hollow and cap them with drives; each affects cardinal neighbors only.
Place one instrument port, one or more cold inlets and one or more hot outlets on non-edge sides.
Multiple cold and hot ports are allowed; place them on valid side blocks to suit the pipe layout.
Seal every outside wall. Windows may replace casing on non-edge side blocks.
Check the instrument port with a Create Wrench. Load fuel only after the structure forms.
Experimental Reactor: Fuel and Control Rods
Fuel and control columns can be placed in different positions and numbers; layout sets heat and control coverage.
Loaded fuel columns strengthen one another across cardinal neighbors; diagonal neighbors do not interact.
Overclocking raises heat and fuel use; more neighboring fuel columns strengthen the feedback.
Control rods limit only cardinally adjacent fuel columns; deeper insertion means lower power.
With multiple neighboring rods, their insertion depths are averaged; one fully inserted rod is not enough to stop the column.
Insert all neighboring control rods to stop that fuel column; redstone shutdown works through rod insertion.
A loaded column with no neighboring control rod runs at full power, even during SCRAM.
Rods and redstone cannot stop these columns or remove fuel while it produces heat; wait for exhaustion.
Experimental Reactor: Run and Stop
Before starting, connect the coolant loop and confirm the fuel is loaded.
Raise the rods gradually to start fission. Deeper insertion means lower power.
Cold coolant absorbs heat and leaves through the hot port. Keep both directions open.
Engineer Goggles show heat production, cooling rate, and coolant stock at the instrument port.
Fully insert the control rods to stop. A redstone signal at the instrument port inserts every movable rod.
Fission stops before residual heat does. Keep coolant circulating until the core cools.
Without an administrator in control, removing the signal returns the rods to their previous target depths.
Experimental Reactor: Load and Replace Fuel
Each refueling port serves the fuel column directly below it and holds one assembly.
With a formed reactor and a non-fissioning column, right-click the port with a fresh enriched uranium fuel assembly.
Exhausted fuel is returned as a Cooled Spent Fuel Assembly.
Insert the neighboring control rod and wait for fission to stop in the target column. Keep cooling residual heat.
Hold fresh fuel and right-click once to replace an exhausted assembly and receive the old one. An assembly with durability remaining cannot be quick-swapped.
Power a Create Mechanical Arm to take fresh fuel from supply and deliver spent fuel to receiving storage. Hoppers cannot access the fuel port.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.enrichmen: The centrifuge separates uranium slurry into low-enriched uranium dust, depleted uranium dust, and recoverable water.
The machine is two blocks tall. Leave room above for the inlet pipe.
Power the centrifuge from below. Processing starts once the speed is stable.
Uranium slurry can only enter from the top.
Higher stable speeds process slurry faster. Keep both powder outputs and water recovery clear.
Both halves can output powder or water from any of their four sides. Use brass funnels to collect the powders separately and pipes to recover water.
Processing pauses if power is lost, speed is unstable, or outputs are blocked. Progress is preserved.
When the bearing wears out, stop the power. Hold one heavy bearing and right-click the front of the lower section to repair it.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.high_pres: High-pressure boiler: Build and zones
By default, length, width, and height are each 5–16 blocks and can be adjusted separately. This example is 7×7×7.
Place the built-in heat exchangers on the base. Hot inlets share this layer and may replace non-corner bottom-edge casing.
Complete the partition with reheating sections and casing. Cold outlets share its layer and stay off the edges.
Leave at least one layer above and below the partition. Place water and controller ports in the water zone.
Place steam ports in the steam zone. Side ports face horizontally outward.
Place safety valves on non-edge roof blocks and keep each outlet clear. Add water, steam, and coolant ports as needed.
Effective heat loops equal the smaller count of built-in heat exchangers and reheating sections.
High-pressure boiler: Connect and run
By default, length, width, and height are each 5–16 blocks and can be adjusted separately.
Water-zone volume determines water capacity; steam-zone volume determines steam capacity.
Fill the water zone first. Then circulate coolant on separate lines.
Start the cold-coolant return before supplying heat. A blocked return limits further heat intake.
With water supplied and cold return flowing, start the hot-coolant input to heat the boiler.
With other conditions equal, a larger water zone warms more slowly.
Water boils before steam is reheated; a larger steam zone pressurizes more slowly.
Use goggles to check boiler status, temperature, pressure, and effective heat loops.
High-pressure boiler: Steam output and pressure
Both steam types can leave the boiler actively through legal industrial pipes. These outlet lines need no external pump.
New steam is classified by actual temperature and pressure. Ordinary and supercritical steam use separate inventories.
Both inventories share zone capacity and boiler pressure. Changing the minimum does not change stored steam types.
Choose a steam type at each outlet with Create's native option. Each drains only its selected inventory; no downgrade conversion occurs.
The minimum output pressure ranges from 0–100. Lower it to 10%. It gates normal output; it is not a target boiler pressure or safety-valve pressure.

create_nuclear_industry.ponder.steam_tur: Steam turbine: Build
Place both end shafts, then keep the rotor row continuous through the center.
Hold casing and right-click the core to fit the front end ring.
Right-click placed casing to extend the shell along the shaft.
Continue adding one shell ring at a time.
Extend the shell toward the rear end.
Close the rear end with its casing ring.
Place the inlet in a legal middle-row side slot.
The exhaust port sits beside the front end ring.
Use a legal side window to inspect the rotor row.
Small turbine: 3×5×3, with 3 rotors.
Medium tier: 5×8×5, with 6 rotors.
Large turbine: 7×11×7, with 9 rotors.
Steam turbine: Steam and output
Feed supercritical steam through the inlet and drain ordinary steam from the exhaust. A boiler outlet can feed industrial pipes actively; pumping from a tank is another option.
Supercritical steam passes through the turbine and converts to an equal amount of steam.
Exhaust steam can be sent to a heat exchanger for condensation and water return.
If exhaust is blocked, the tiny turnover space fills and further intake stops. Keep the return line open to continue producing power.
The front output shaft runs at 256 RPM.
The rear shaft shares the front shaft's total stress capacity.
Steam turbine: Flow and efficiency
Small turbine at 10 mB/t: below 30%, it still consumes steam but produces no power.
The small turbine starts producing power at 16.2 mB/t, at 0.5× efficiency.
The small turbine reaches 1.2× efficiency at its rated flow of 54 mB/t.
Medium tier is rated at 108 mB/t, up to 1.5× efficiency.
The large turbine is rated at 216 mB/t, up to 1.8× efficiency.
Efficiency uses actual average exhaust over 40 ticks, not the amount stored in the inlet tank.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.nuclear_h: Nuclear heat exchanger: Faces and inline connection
Hot coolant enters the rear and cold coolant leaves the front.
The heated top face can connect to a heat load. Facing determines the hot and cold ports.
Place two exchangers in line and connect the outer ends to share hot and cold coolant; each top face can provide heat.
Nuclear heat exchanger: Powering a steam engine
Hot coolant enters the rear and cold coolant leaves the front; the exchanger heats the boiler from below.
The boiler tank touches a steam engine; heat from below lets the engine produce power.
The exchanger sits below the boiler and supplies heat upward while hot coolant flows.
At the small tank's operating heat level, the steam engine piston reciprocates and turns the shaft.
Residual heat sustains output briefly after hot coolant runs out; the steam engine and shaft stop when it fades.
Nuclear heat exchanger: Built into a boiler
Place an exchanger inside the bottom layer, away from the frame.
Place a reheating section in the partition above; effective heat loops equal the smaller of the two counts.
The hot-coolant inlet shares the exchanger's bottom layer, and the cold-coolant outlet sits beside the partition; connect their lines separately.
Nuclear heat exchanger: Processing heat
A basin can stay superheated on top, and an empty basin still uses heat; equal coolant returns as hot fluid falls.
The empty sintering furnace is already heated; add a green fuel pellet for processing into a sintered fuel pellet.
The default is 4 mB/t; heating stops immediately if hot coolant runs out or the cold return is blocked.
When coolant circulation returns, the furnace heats up and processing resumes.
Nuclear heat exchanger: Steam condensation
Steam enters from the rear and condensed water leaves the front; steam and recovered water change 1:1 by default.
Direct contact with snow, ice, or packed ice condenses steam and melts into water; the water source eventually evaporates. Flowing water is invalid.
Blue ice supplies cold indefinitely without being consumed; condensation pauses if it is removed or the water return is blocked.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.fuel_sint: Fuel Sintering Furnace: Sintering and Heat
Supply heat from below and insert green fuel pellets from the top.
When sintering finishes, collect the product from a side. Use goggles to check processing progress.
Sintering pauses when heat is lost and continues when heating resumes.
Fuel Sintering Furnace: Automation and Nuclear Heat
Feed green fuel pellets through a chute on top.
All four horizontal sides allow sintered fuel pellets to be extracted. Use a funnel to send them into a receiving container.

A nuclear heat exchanger can also supply heat from below: hot coolant enters at the rear, and an equal amount of cold coolant leaves at the front. Maintain the hot coolant supply and keep the cold coolant outlet clear.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.shielded_: Shielded Assembly Station: Placement and Ports
Leave a 2×2×2 space. Placing one station item creates the complete machine.
Drive only the shaft below the master block, at a minimum of 32 RPM.
The horizontal sides accept materials or release products. The top accepts inputs only, and the bottom has no item port.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.dry_stora: Dry Storage Rack: Storage and Automation
Right-click with a sealed nuclear waste cask to insert one. Casks containing either spent fuel or accident waste can be stored.
Right-click with an empty hand to retrieve one cask. If your inventory is full, the cask stays in the rack.
The top and four sides accept inputs; every face allows outputs. The bottom only allows outputs. The east hopper feeds the rack, and the bottom hopper extracts southward.
Occupancy rises as casks arrive. Goggles show used slots and capacity. The default is 16 casks and can be configured; this rack currently holds 16/16.
A full rack rejects further inputs. The extra cask waits in the upstream hopper.
Removing one cask frees a slot, allowing the upstream cask to enter. The retrieved cask remains in the southern receiving barrel.

create_nuclear_industry.ponder.experimen: Stop fission in the target column and remove its fuel before maintenance. Hold a steel plate and right-click the refueling port to repair the fuel column; residual heat still needs cooling.
Use a steel plate on the control-rod drive to repair its column and release a jam once integrity is sufficient. Repairs do not restore fuel or erase stored heat.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.high_pres: Stored, heat-qualified supercritical steam can drain to the shared minimum below the new-steam classification pressure. Its type stays unchanged; keep steam types on separate lines.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.steam_tur: After steam stops, wait 40 ticks; power stops when the average falls below threshold.
Redstone at the controller stops this turbine's power immediately. This differs from steam loss fading through the averaging window and does not remove other generators' power.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.high_pres: High-pressure boiler: Relief and safety
Place multiple safety valves on non-edge roof blocks. Keep the block directly above each valve clear; goggles show clear valves and total vent capacity.
By default, valves open at 90% pressure and close at 80%. Each clear valve vents up to 512 mB/t, regardless of boiler volume.
Blocking one valve stops only that valve. The other clear valve still vents; add effective valves and keep every outlet clear.
All blocked valves mean no pressure relief. Stop heat and clear the steam path; the output minimum is neither a safety-valve setting nor a target pressure.
Redstone at the controller stops new heat intake. No hot coolant or a blocked cold return also stops intake, but existing fluids and residual heat remain.
With no water and walls at boiling temperature, 20 seconds of dry firing destroys one heat exchanger or reheating section by default. Maintain water, stop heat and cool before maintenance.
Dry-firing damage does not drop an intact machine. Remove the hazard, replace the damaged part and check the structure again.
Default rated pressure is 100%. Exceeding it accumulates up to 10 seconds of tolerance; reaching 150% bursts immediately through a random face. Higher pressure increases the danger range.
By default, pressure must remain at or below 95% for 2 seconds to clear accumulated overpressure time. A brief dip does not restart the danger clock.

Dismantling a dangerous boiler triggers its accident immediately, with overpressure bursting first. Stop heat, depressurize and cool before normal dismantling. Boiler accidents do not produce nuclear waste.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.experimen: Reactor: Accidents and recovery
Loss of cooling and heat buildup damage fuel columns and control rods. Watch the instrument with goggles and keep coolant circulating after shutdown until residual heat subsides.
A completed meltdown countdown causes an accident, and dismantling a dangerous structure triggers one immediately. Shut down, cool the core and check dismantling conditions first.
TNT or creepers actually breaking members of a still-dangerous reactor can also trigger an accident. Nearby explosions and cold empty reactors do not trigger one indiscriminately.
Hot wreckage and molten corium cause contact heat damage and ignition. Fire resistance and radiation protection act separately; a suit does not replace protection from heat.
Extinguish the fire spots directly. Putting out fire does not cool the wreckage or remove waste radiation.
Molten corium continues moving and corroding downward. Buckets and pumps cannot recover it; wait for solidification. Cooling pauses while unloaded.
Adjacent water speeds solidification and solid cooling. Solidified material may still be hot; cooling removes heat danger, not the waste radiation.
After solidification and cooling, use an ordinary pickaxe to recover the accident waste inside. Empty wreckage creates neither waste nor radiation.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.reactor_a: Install an automation port on a non-edge side position of the reactor.
Place an adjacent Blaze Burner to serve as administrator. For a cold start, fuel it first and connect reactor cooling.
Invert the burner run-permission signal before connecting it to the instrument SCRAM. Losing permission then sends a shutdown signal to the instrument.
Empty-hand right-click the assigned burner to open its three-page interface. Right-click with held fuel to refuel it.
The Overview page shows mode, target and actual heat, rod positions and coolant stocks. Edit mode and values, then press Apply to submit them.
Apply does not replace Start. Start separately when ready; Stop is available on all pages. Closing the interface does not pause the reactor.
The Core page is a read-only cross section of fuel, integrity, stored heat and jams. Loading fuel and steel-plate maintenance still use world ports.
The Protection page shows interlocks and reset conditions. It cannot disable thresholds; closing discards unapplied edits.
Uniform Depth applies a target to all movable rods. While running, individual adjustments remain available when safety checks permit.
Constant Heat adjusts rods toward a HU/t target; watch actual and reachable heat. Individual rod controls are read-only in this mode and in safety shutdown states.
Reactor heat can sustain ordinary administrator burning, consuming 1 HU/t by default. Inadequate energy still revokes run permission.
Empty or exhausted columns do not alone stop the whole reactor while usable fuel remains. Reachable heat changes with the available fuel.
Cooling shortages and heat buildup take priority over targets. Exhausted fuel, missing rod coverage, jams, lost contact and SCRAM also require attention.
Faults and SCRAM remain stopped. Remove the cause, meet the stable healthy conditions and confirm Reset manually. Removing redstone alone does not restart rod withdrawal.
Normal save and reload rechecks safety before resuming the mode and rod positions. Manual shutdown, faults and SCRAM remain stopped.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.radiation: Fresh assemblies, uranium raw materials and depleted uranium materials or equipment do not radiate. Once fuel starts being consumed, an assembly radiates even while durability remains.
Cooled Spent Fuel Assemblies and accident waste are also radiation sources. Cooling does not make them nonradioactive.
Hold the radiation meter in either hand to read field strength, accumulated dose and absorbed intensity. Watch readings when approaching, moving or shielding sources.
Wear the suit in its proper slots to reduce your absorption. The hood also works as Engineer Goggles. Wearing it does not reduce a carried source's radiation toward others.
Ordinary chests and barrels provide no extra shielding. Nuclear waste inside them still exposes nearby people.
Shielding concrete reduces radiation passing through it, and a complete reactor shell shields internal sources. Arbitrary decorative blocks are not shielding.
Seal spent fuel or accident waste at the shielded assembly station, then store the nuclear waste cask in a dry rack.
A sealed cask reduces outgoing radiation by 95% by default. A complete dry rack fully shields its casks; outside it, only the cask shielding remains.
After leaving or shielding the source, accumulated dose gradually recovers. Handle cooling, burns and radiation separately; a cool appearance does not prove radiation safety.
create_nuclear_industry.ponder.experimen: Seal accident waste at the shielded assembly station, then store the nuclear waste cask in a dry rack. Recovering or shielding the source reduces the field nearby.
